A1.justification: Despite the changed title and organization, both PDFs describe the same Mahalanobis OOD geometry study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-model OOD evaluations, dimension ablations, geometric correlations and regression-based normalization experiments in Sections 3–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and reports new ID-only normalization-selection results and controlled stability experiments in Sections 6–7 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: v1's auxiliary-OOD-trained regression predictor is replaced by an ID-only rule selecting an interior turning point of the LID–spectral-slope proxy, with a fallback (v3 Section 6.4 and Appendix D.4). The radial transformation remains unchanged. The documented scoring pipeline also changes from whitening before transformation and mapping class means (v1 Appendix C.3) to transforming features before fitting Gaussian statistics (v3 Appendix D.2).

E1.justification: Both retain ImageNet-based vision OOD detection with NINCO, iNaturalist, SSB-Hard, OpenImages-O and Textures. The new selector and stability analyses use the existing representations; they do not introduce another dataset, domain or detection task.

E2.justification: The explicit NINCO comparison expands from Mahalanobis variants in v1 Table 4 to include MSP, MLS, KNN and VIM in v3 Table 7. These comparators already appeared in v1's aggregate comparison. Tabulated oracle MD*/RMD* comparisons disappear from the corresponding aggregate and NINCO tables, although oracle-relative errors remain plotted.

E3.justification: Leave-one-OOD-dataset-out regression validation is replaced by held-out-ID selection of one β per model, applied across OOD benchmarks. The stated search range changes from [-2, 3] to [-2, 2], retaining 0.25 steps, although v3 Figure 6 still displays values reaching 3. Appendix E adds controlled rotation, allocation and covariance interventions. The detailed normalization tables also omit the previously included ViT In21K configuration.

E4.justification: v3 adds numerical factorization checks, size–stretch compensation analysis, orthogonal-rotation interventions, allocation smoothing, spectrum shaping and fixed-covariance rescaling checks. It also examines proxy tracking, neighborhood-size sensitivity and the additional explanatory contribution of LID (Section 7 and Appendix E). The earlier dimension ablations and spectral-shift analyses are retained, partly relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions use cross-model/dataset distributions without specifying seeds, repeated-run counts or significance tests. v3 adds model-level correlation IQRs in Table 4 and an undefined shaded band in Figure 13. The IQRs describe model heterogeneity, but the band could represent sampling uncertainty or descriptive spread; its unspecified meaning prevents a reliable judgment about changes in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New proxy-selected FPR results replace regression-selected results, and stability-analysis outcomes are added. For example, BEiTV2 In21k's learned MD result of 27.4% in v1 Table 3 is replaced by RS-MD at 29.8% in v3 Table 6 under the changed selection procedure. Regression MAE/R² and tabulated oracle results disappear. The original cross-model MD/RMD table is identical, while NINCO BEiTV2 In1k RMD changes from 45.7% to 45.6%.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained eigenbasis and radial pullback derivations, v3 introduces exact size–stretch factorization, a log-score variance decomposition, the spectrum–allocation identity and fixed-covariance scale invariance. It states positivity assumptions and treats RMD through its separate quadratic components rather than assuming one shared quadratic form (Section 7 and Appendix E).

C1.justification: The practical tuning contribution changes from predicting β without target OOD access, while learning from auxiliary OOD datasets, to selecting β without any OOD samples. v3 foregrounds this stronger access claim in its abstract, introduction and conclusion, replacing v1's future-work proposal for model-free selection. The core representation-dependence and geometry–performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds a mechanism based on spectral weighting, sample allocation and compensation between size and stretch. It explicitly characterizes the geometric proxy as lossy, distinguishes across-model correlations from within-model β optima, and explains why RMD requires term-wise analysis. These substantially extend v1's mainly correlational interpretation of manifold complexity and cluster compactness.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies ImageNet training/validation roles, held-out-ID tuning, k=50 for the selected LID proxy, last-layer features, regularization and zero-deviation handling, and no-intercept fitting for the stability proxy. The checkpoint/source mapping is unchanged. Important implementation quantities, including held-out sample size, regularization strength and the fallback threshold, remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The auxiliary-outlier-exposure analogy and its Hendrycks et al. (2018) citation disappear with the regression framework. The remaining related-work coverage is substantially retained, with a refined distinction between changing the scoring rule, fixed spherical normalization and adjustable radial geometry.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, conclusion and much of the explanatory narrative are rewritten. Background becomes a separate section, the original main-text spectral analysis moves to Appendix C, appendices are reorganized, and RS-MD/RS-RMD terminology replaces the learned-selector notation. This is substantial restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns. Correlation heatmaps become dot plots, result tables gain revised structure and colored highlighting, and spectral figures are relocated or consolidated. New proxy-trajectory and stability figures and diagnostic tables are added. Several original plots are retained; percentage conversion alone is not treated as a result change.

improvement.justification: v3 better aligns its ID-only tuning claim with a concrete procedure, replacing v1's auxiliary-OOD-trained predictor, and adds useful mathematical decompositions and controlled mechanism checks. However, the selector's fallback remains underspecified, Figure 6 conflicts with the stated β range, and Table 7 retains an obsolete regression caption. The new proxy-tracking evidence is also heterogeneous (Table 4). These unresolved validation and reporting gaps limit an otherwise positive net quality gain.
